content:
⚖️ Once you become an advocate, you become a student of law for life.

There is something profoundly beautiful about the legal profession — you never really stop learning.

Every case teaches you something new.
Every argument challenges your perspective.
Every judgment reminds you that the law is not merely about sections and precedents, but about people, justice, and society.

This quote by Fali S. Nariman captures that journey perfectly:

“Once you become an advocate, you become a student of law for life.”

And perhaps that is what makes being a lawyer so different.

You may graduate from law school, but you never graduate from learning the law.

As a law professional, I’m slowly beginning to understand that becoming a good legal professional isn’t about knowing everything. It is about having the curiosity to keep asking questions, the humility to keep learning, and the courage to keep evolving.

Because the law changes.
Society changes.
Arguments change.
And we must change with them.

So, here’s to being a student of law - today, tomorrow, and for life. ⚖️📚

What is one lesson law has taught you that goes beyond textbooks?

comment: The deeper challenge in law is not just keeping up with new judgments, but learning when a legal principle needs to evolve with changing social realities and lived experiences.
